Why PGX

A database cheap enough to allocate like an object.

Agents, test suites, CI jobs and preview environments create databases constantly and throw them away minutes later. Giving each one its own PostgreSQL server costs a process, tens of megabytes and a cold start. PGX runs a single process that holds many isolated databases — immutable state is shared, so each database pays mainly for what makes it different.

The usual way1 database → 1 PostgreSQL server
With PGX1 runtime → thousands of databases

Measured on a 4 vCPU / 8 GB VPS with ZFS block cloning; the load generator shared the CPUs, so these describe the architecture, not a capacity limit. Every figure has a committed script and raw result — see the benchmark suite.

How it works

Sealed template in, disposable database out.

Seal a template

Build a database once and seal it as an immutable template.

Mint a database

Branch it in milliseconds — copy-on-write where the backend supports it.

Use it

An agent, CI job or test suite runs against a real Postgres database.

Discard

A TTL or grace period drops it automatically. Permanent databases stay.

PGX speaks the PostgreSQL wire protocol and SQL dialect, so Rails, Django, Prisma, SQLAlchemy and node-postgres run their full migrate → test → schema-change lifecycles on it unchanged.

Beta — for disposable databases.

PGX is in public beta and built for disposable development, test and CI databases. It is not intended to be the production primary store for your data.
